title: 2001 Miami Dolphins season
summary: The document covers the 2001 Miami Dolphins season, the franchise's 32nd NFL season and 36th in the AFC, and their second under head coach Dave Wannstedt. It outlines the team's overall performance, including their 11–5 record and second-place finish in the AFC East, along with their season-ending 20–3 loss to the defending Super Bowl champion Baltimore Ravens in the Wild Card round of the playoffs. The document highlights the team's offensive and defensive rankings (8th in points scored, 11th in points allowed), their problematic turnover differential (-13 for the season, with 41 giveaways), and quarterback Jay Fiedler's struggles with 19 interceptions and six fumbles. It also notes embarrassing regular season losses to the New York Jets, San Francisco 49ers, and St. Louis Rams, as well as the franchise's subsequent playoff drought until 2008. The document is organized into standard sections including offseason (NFL draft and undrafted free agents), staff, roster, preseason, regular season (schedule and standings), and playoffs. The playoff section provides a detailed game summary of the Wild Card loss to Baltimore, describing the Ravens' dominant rushing attack (222 yards), the Dolphins' offensive struggles (151 total yards), key plays including Terry Allen's touchdown run, Elvis Grbac's 99-yard scoring drive, turnovers, and Matt Stover's field goals that sealed the victory. The document concludes with notes and references sections.
